architecture/code-architecture.md.title: ForgeGate Code Architecture

architecture/policy/adaptive-autonomy.md.title: Adaptive Autonomy
architecture/policy/adaptive-autonomy.md.first_paragraph: Not fully autonomous in every uncertain case; not constantly asking user. Policy-driven, context-sensitive.

architecture/policy/adaptive-routing.md.title: Adaptive Routing
architecture/policy/adaptive-routing.md.first_paragraph: Not "first healthy wins". Quality/latency-aware with controlled degradation.

architecture/policy/client-capabilities..title: Client Capability Awareness

architecture/policy/routing-actions.md.title: Routing Actions

architecture/product/separation.md.title: Separation of Concerns

architecture/recovery/action-uncertainty.title: Action Uncertainty
architecture/recovery/action-uncertainty.first_paragraph: Connection failure does not prove action did not execute.

architecture/recovery/checkpoints.md.title: Stable Execution Checkpoints
architecture/recovery/checkpoints.md.first_paragraph: Conceptual stable checkpoints summarize latest known-good task execution state. Make recovery cheap and reliable.

architecture/recovery/facts-vs-interpret.title: Facts vs Interpretation
architecture/recovery/facts-vs-interpret.first_paragraph: Distinguish verified execution evidence from model interpretation.
must_lines: Recovery prioritizes verified facts. LLM summary must not overwrite/contradict known facts.

architecture/recovery/handoff.md.title: Structured Execution Handoff
architecture/recovery/handoff.md.first_paragraph: Not raw full replay, not one giant master prompt, not LLM summary only.

architecture/recovery/recovery-input.md.title: Recovery Input
architecture/recovery/recovery-input.md.first_paragraph: Replacement model receives: latest stable checkpoint; significant events since checkpoint; current workspace/session state; concise semantic handoff summary.

architecture/recovery/status.md.title: Recovery Strategy Status
architecture/recovery/status.md.first_paragraph: DECIDED: - transparent request-level failover before commit. - no model-stream splicing after commit. - structured task-level recovery after commit. - structured handoff rather than giant master prompt. - checkpoint + facts + workspace state + semantic summary. - explicit distinction between facts and model interpretation. - unknown side-effect state must be reconciled before retry. - recovery route must respect task/model compatibility.
must_lines: unknown side-effect state must be reconciled before retry.
recovery route must respect task/model compatibility.

architecture/recovery/task-recovery.md.title: Task-Level Recovery
architecture/recovery/task-recovery.md.first_paragraph: If model/provider disappears during ongoing task, preserve useful execution state. Replacement model receives structured execution handoff, NOT blind restart from original user prompt.

architecture/recovery/transactional-boun.title: Transactional Response Boundary
architecture/recovery/transactional-boun.first_paragraph: Distinguish pre-commit and committed response state.

architecture/runtime/multi-session.md.title: Multi-Session Concurrency
architecture/runtime/multi-session.md.first_paragraph: Baseline requirement: 4+ concurrent agent sessions from start. Not a future optimization.
must_lines: Routing must account globally for provider limits (max concurrency, RPM, TPM, hourly budgets, cooldowns). Avoid per-session provider logic unaware of global capacity.

architecture/runtime/project-session.md.title: Project / Workspace and Session Hierarchy
architecture/runtime/project-session.md.first_paragraph: Hierarchy: ForgeGate Instance → Project / Workspace → Session / Chat / Track.

architecture/runtime/public-api.md.title: Public API
architecture/runtime/public-api.md.first_paragraph: Public endpoint remains ordinary OpenAI-compatible: POST /v1/chat/completions

architecture/runtime/session-identity.md.title: Internal Session Identity
architecture/runtime/session-identity.md.first_paragraph: OpenAI Chat Completions does not guarantee a stable conversation ID. ForgeGate needs a Session Resolver using available signals: correlation metadata, conversation/request metadata, message-history fingerprint, workspace paths from tool context, recent request continuity, other stable client signals.
must_lines: Exact fingerprint algorithm NOT decided. Session identity and workspace identity are separate; same workspace with different sessions must not collapse.

architecture/runtime/single-instance.md.title: Single-Instance Concurrent Runtime
architecture/runtime/single-instance.md.first_paragraph: One server/process instance supports multiple projects/workspaces and multiple chat/agent sessions concurrently.
must_lines: Concrete ConcurrentDictionary/Semaphore details must not leak into core logic.

architecture/supervision/cross-session.m.title: Cross-Session Protection
architecture/supervision/cross-session.m.first_paragraph: Detect actions that may destroy/interfere with another active track.
must_lines: Example: Session A modifies foo.cs; Session B proposes reverting/stashing it. ForgeGate must attribute changes to Session A and prevent Session B from treating them as unexplained noise.

architecture/supervision/execution-super.title: Execution Supervision
architecture/supervision/execution-super.first_paragraph: Supervise pathological/wasteful behavior, not only dangerous actions.

architecture/supervision/hierarchical-co.title: Hierarchical Supervision Configuration
architecture/supervision/hierarchical-co.first_paragraph: Effective behavior influenced by multiple scopes (not finalized merge semantics): Instance defaults → Workspace overrides → Model profile → Virtual routing profile → Session/task overrides.

architecture/supervision/long-running-co.title: Long-Running Command Semantics
must_lines: Long-running (e.g., npm run dev) must not be treated as failure due to non-exit. Avoid repeated restarts; use existing process state/output. Exact tracking not decided.

architecture/supervision/session-observa.title: Session Observability
architecture/supervision/session-observa.first_paragraph: Internal logs/traces of agent activity, queryable by policy logic, reasoners, supervisors, admin UI, audit.

architecture/supervision/soft-ownership..title: Soft Ownership + Escalation
architecture/supervision/soft-ownership..first_paragraph: No hard file locking. Soft activity attribution / intent is maintained.

architecture/supervision/supervision-pro.title: Configurable Supervision Profiles
architecture/supervision/supervision-pro.first_paragraph: Supervision intensity is not globally fixed. Different models need different control levels.

architecture/task/adaptive-task.md.title: Adaptive Task Management
architecture/task/adaptive-task.md.first_paragraph: Task management intensity depends on: model behavior profile, task complexity, observed drift, current execution behavior, supervision configuration.

architecture/task/bounded.md.title: Bounded Prompt Injection
architecture/task/bounded.md.first_paragraph: No unbounded supervision text. Additions must be minimal, relevant, deduplicated, scoped, removable when no longer needed.
must_lines: No unbounded supervision text. Additions must be minimal, relevant, deduplicated, scoped, removable when no longer needed.

architecture/task/classification.md.title: Task Classification
architecture/task/classification.md.first_paragraph: Adaptive classification. Not mandatory for every request.
must_lines: Simple tasks must stay simple without metadata.

architecture/task/declared-vs-effective..title: Declared vs Effective Task Profile
architecture/task/declared-vs-effective..first_paragraph: Explicit metadata = declared profile. Runtime may maintain different effective profile.

architecture/task/injection-intensity.md.title: Injection Intensity
architecture/task/injection-intensity.md.first_paragraph: Depends on: model behavior profile; effective task profile; recent policy violations; observed drift; workspace state; supervision configuration.

architecture/task/injection.md.title: Adaptive Prompt / Context Injection
architecture/task/injection.md.first_paragraph: Allowed to modify upstream context. Must NOT inject one large global system prompt blindly.
must_lines: Allowed to modify upstream context. Must NOT inject one large global system prompt blindly.

architecture/task/progress.md.title: Progress Supervision
architecture/task/progress.md.first_paragraph: No universal progress metric yet. Progress may include: source mutation, new diagnostic evidence, test/build results, narrowed hypothesis, discovered call site, verified assumption, completed milestone, useful plan refinement.

architecture/task/provenance.md.title: Context Provenance
architecture/task/provenance.md.first_paragraph: Distinguish sources: user-authored instructions; client/system instructions; ForgeGate policy context; ForgeGate task context; ForgeGate runtime correction context.
must_lines: Must not collapse into indistinguishable blob. Exact representation and message-role strategy NOT decided.

architecture/task/reassessment.md.title: Runtime Task Reassessment
architecture/task/reassessment.md.first_paragraph: Task type, complexity, supervision intensity, routing requirements may evolve during execution.

architecture/task/supervision-summary.md.title: Adaptive Supervision Summary
architecture/task/supervision-summary.md.first_paragraph: Not one mechanism. Combines: deterministic policy checks; behavior detectors; Task Manager; semantic policy reasoner; task analyzer; adaptive prompt/context injection; workspace coordination; cross-session signals.

architecture/task/task-correction.md.title: Task Manager as Corrective Supervision
architecture/task/task-correction.md.first_paragraph: Task Manager activates when bad execution behavior is detected.

architecture/task/task-manager.md.title: Adaptive Task Manager
architecture/task/task-manager.md.first_paragraph: Conceptual Task Manager / TaskExecutionContext. Not a mandatory rigid TODO list for every request. Preserves and supervises task intent.

behavior/certification-integrity.md.title: Certification Integrity
behavior/certification-integrity.md.first_paragraph: Detect invalid patterns: `cmd | tail/head/grep` then treating `$?` as tested command's exit code; manually printing PASS/exit-code strings; using broad suites as substitutes for specifically requested focused proof.
must_lines: Evidence must derive from actual command/runtime results.

behavior/completion-verification.md.title: Completion Verification
behavior/completion-verification.md.first_paragraph: Distinct conceptual concern (separate from routing, policy, planning, workspace coordination).

behavior/evidence-hierarchy.md.title: Evidence Hierarchy
must_lines: Lower class must not be promoted. Static presence != runtime proof; test proof != visual proof; inferred state != observed UI state. Observed runtime evidence overrides contradictory static assumptions.

behavior/facts-vs-claims.md.title: Facts vs Claims
behavior/facts-vs-claims.md.first_paragraph: Distinguish: execution fact (command exit 1); model interpretation (failure appears unrelated); completion claim (task PASS).
must_lines: Final claim must be justified by available evidence and policy.

behavior/investigation-supervision.md.title: Investigation Supervision
behavior/investigation-supervision.md.first_paragraph: Anti-patterns: repeated instrumentation without narrowing unknown; revisiting closed causal boundaries; multiple hypotheses in one slice; inventing fixes before root cause proven; using observation channel already known inaccessible.

behavior/long-running-awareness.md.title: Long-Running Execution Awareness
behavior/long-running-awareness.md.first_paragraph: Agents may run dev servers, wait indefinitely for non-terminating processes, restart same process after continuation, kill healthy cold builds due to arbitrary timeouts.

behavior/mvp-boundary.md.title: MVP Boundary
behavior/mvp-boundary.md.first_paragraph: Do NOT implement all 30 rules in MVP.

behavior/requirements-source.md.title: Behavioral Requirements Source
behavior/requirements-source.md.first_paragraph: Supervision driven by observed real-world agent failure patterns (uploaded "AGENT EXECUTION FAILURE PATTERNS — ORCHESTRATOR RULES").

behavior/status-vocabulary.md.title: Canonical Execution Statuses
behavior/status-vocabulary.md.first_paragraph: PASS (required behavior directly proven); PARTIAL_PASS (partly complete); FAIL (directly observed incorrect); NOT_PROVEN (insufficient evidence / competing explanations); NOT_RUN (not attempted); BLOCKED (attempted but concrete external/technical blocker prevents completion).
must_lines: BLOCKED must never substitute for NOT_RUN.

behavior/status.md.title: Behavioral Decisions Status
behavior/status.md.first_paragraph: DECIDED: - hybrid buffered streaming; evidence hierarchy; canonical completion statuses; completion verification separate concern; observed failure patterns drive supervision; not all supervision in LLM reasoning; deterministic rules for obvious cases; semantic supervision for ambiguous/contextual cases.

behavior/unsafe-recovery.md.title: Unsafe Workspace Recovery
behavior/unsafe-recovery.md.first_paragraph: Dangerous actions: git stash, reset, restore, checkout --, clean; broad rm/rm -rf. Especially dangerous with multiple ForgeGate sessions on same workspace.
must_lines: Cross-session attribution and soft ownership must be considered before workspace recovery actions.

capacity/coordinator.md.title: Central Capacity Coordinator
capacity/coordinator.md.first_paragraph: Single-instance MVP uses one central in-process Capacity Coordinator. Coordinates concurrent sessions globally before upstream provider calls.

capacity/future-distributed.md.title: Future Distributed Capacity
capacity/future-distributed.md.first_paragraph: MVP remains single-process/in-process. No Redis or distributed locks. Capacity Coordinator kept behind clean application boundary so distributed implementation can be introduced later without rewriting routing semantics.

capacity/reconciliation.md.title: Capacity Reconciliation
capacity/reconciliation.md.first_paragraph: Before provider call: reserve estimated capacity. After completion: reconcile against actual provider usage when available; local estimates otherwise; observed failures (e.g., rate limits). Perfect token prediction NOT required. Not a billing engine.

compatibility/adjustment.md.title: Compatibility Adjustment
compatibility/adjustment.md.first_paragraph: Retain observable adjustments: parameter translated; advisory parameter dropped; semantic requirement unsupported. Supports audit, debugging, admin visibility. Exact DTO/event design deferred.

compatibility/mismatch.md.title: Capability Mismatch
compatibility/mismatch.md.first_paragraph: First-class route eligibility reason. Examples: requires tools + route lacks tools → INELIGIBLE; requires vision + route lacks vision → INELIGIBLE; required context exceeds route context → INELIGIBLE. Do NOT silently send semantically incompatible request.

compatibility/normalization.md.title: Parameter Normalization
compatibility/normalization.md.first_paragraph: If provider supports safe equivalent representation, translate parameter. Example: max_completion_tokens → provider equivalent max_tokens when semantics sufficiently equivalent. Translation = compatibility adjustment, not silent loss.

compatibility/parameters.md.title: Parameter Compatibility Policy
compatibility/parameters.md.first_paragraph: Not "unsupported → silently drop everything". Not fail on every optional parameter. Explicit parameter compatibility policy.

compatibility/unsupported.md.title: Unsupported Semantic Requirements
compatibility/unsupported.md.first_paragraph: If parameter represents required semantic contract route cannot provide, do NOT silently remove. Example: strict structured JSON/schema requirement + route cannot guarantee/support → route ineligible or explicit compatibility error. May participate in routing eligibility.

Routing logic must not depend directly on EF Core DbContext, Npgsql, HttpClient details, environment variables, ASP.NET HttpContext, concrete provider adapters. Infrastructure implements contracts consumed by higher-level logic. Transport/API DTOs must not leak deeply into application/domain logic.
must_lines: Infrastructure details must not become dependencies of core business logic. Routing logic must not depend directly on EF Core DbContext, Npgsql, HttpClient details, environment variables, ASP.NET HttpContext, concrete provider adapters. Inf

engineering/boundaries/dependency-invers.title: Dependency Inversion
engineering/boundaries/dependency-invers.first_paragraph: Higher-level policy/application defines contracts it needs. Lower-level infrastructure implements them. Application/domain must not depend directly on provider HTTP clients, environment variables, concrete secret stores, EF Core DbContext, Npgsql, concrete provider adapters, concrete HTTP transport details. Concrete implementations wired at composition root.

engineering/cancellation/child-timeouts..title: Child Operation Timeouts
engineering/cancellation/child-timeouts..first_paragraph: Child operation may use linked CancellationToken with bounded timeout when owning boundary requires. Example: request cancellation + provider timeout. Reason for cancellation/timeout must remain distinguishable where needed.
must_lines: Child operation may use linked CancellationToken with bounded timeout when owning boundary requires. Example: request cancellation + provider timeout. Reason for cancellation/timeout must remain distinguishable where needed.

engineering/cancellation/failure-semanti.title: Cancellation Failure Semantics
engineering/cancellation/failure-semanti.first_paragraph: User/client cancellation should not normally be reported as internal system failure. Provider timeout normalizes to provider failure model. Semantic policy/verifier timeout represents supervision degradation, not provider failure. Do NOT collapse every OperationCanceledException into one generic error.

engineering/cancellation/model.md.title: Cancellation Model
engineering/cancellation/model.md.first_paragraph: Structured end-to-end cancellation. Inbound HTTP/request cancellation enters application use case and passes through async I/O boundaries. Async APIs that may wait/block on I/O should accept CancellationToken where appropriate. Do NOT silently drop cancellation propagation.

engineering/cancellation/timeout-ownersh.title: Timeout Ownership
engineering/cancellation/timeout-ownersh.first_paragraph: Timeouts must have explicit owner. Provider request timeout → provider execution concern. Capacity wait budget → routing/capacity concern. Semantic policy timeout → supervision concern. HTTP/client cancellation → caller/request cancellation. Do NOT hide arbitrary timeouts in utility/helper methods.
must_lines: Timeouts must have explicit owner. Provider request timeout → provider execution concern. Capacity wait budget → routing/capacity concern. Semantic policy timeout → supervision concern. HTTP/client cancellation → caller/request cancellation

engineering/components/components.md.title: Small Cohesive Components
engineering/components/components.md.first_paragraph: Prefer small cohesive classes with explicit collaboration. Not maximum class count. Avoid one-method-one-class, interface-for-every-implementation without reason, excessive wrapper/decorator chains, unnecessary generic abstractions. Small meaningful blocks, not abstraction for abstraction's sake.

engineering/config/examples.md.title: Configuration Examples
engineering/config/examples.md.first_paragraph: Bootstrap/static: database connection/bootstrap; server/listen settings; secret-store selection; infrastructure startup defaults; development bootstrap. Runtime operational: providers; model routes; routing profiles; policy settings; admin-editable config. Secrets in SecretStore. Health/cooldowns/current capacity = runtime state.

engineering/config/ownership.md.title: Configuration Ownership
engineering/config/ownership.md.first_paragraph: Layered configuration ownership. Conceptually: appsettings/environment → bootstrap/infrastructure startup config; PostgreSQL → runtime-editable operational config; SecretStore → API keys/credentials; in-memory state owners → ephemeral runtime state.

engineering/config/single-owner.md.title: Single Authoritative Owner for Config
engineering/config/single-owner.md.first_paragraph: A setting must have one authoritative owner. Do NOT allow same operational setting independently editable from appsettings, environment, database, runtime state without explicit precedence rule. When multiple sources intentionally supported, precedence must be documented and deterministic.

engineering/contracts/api-contracts.md.title: API Contracts and OpenAPI
engineering/contracts/api-contracts.md.first_paragraph: ASP.NET Core endpoints must have explicit contracts. OpenAPI/Swagger for developer-facing API discovery and validation. At minimum: documented endpoints; request/response schemas; error contracts; API version/compatibility. OpenAI-compatible surface: compatibility with expected OpenAI shapes takes precedence over prettier ForgeGate-specific public DTOs. Internal Admin APIs may use ForgeGate-native contracts.

engineering/contracts/contract-ownership.title: Contract Ownership
engineering/contracts/contract-ownership.first_paragraph: Contracts/interfaces belong to consumer/policy-owning side, not implementation side. Examples: Application/Secrets/ISecretStore (Infrastructure/Secrets/EnvironmentSecretStore); Application/Capacity/ICapacityCoordinator (Infrastructure/Capacity/InProcessCapacityCoordinator); Application/Sessions/ISessionStore (Infrastructure/Persistence/EfSessionStore). No global ForgeGate.Abstractions dumping ground. No interface for every class.

engineering/contracts/contracts.md.title: Explicit Contracts at External/Replaceable Boundaries
engineering/contracts/contracts.md.first_paragraph: Explicit abstractions around volatile external dependencies: provider transport; secret storage; clock/time for deterministic testing; persistence repositories/query ports; capacity coordination; semantic policy reasoner; external model discovery. Do NOT hide stable internal domain code behind unnecessary interfaces.

engineering/dependencies/agent-rule.md.title: Coding Agent Package Rule
engineering/dependencies/agent-rule.md.first_paragraph: Before adding new external dependency, agent must ask: (1) Is requirement solved by .NET/ASP.NET Core? (2) Does library solve substantial complexity? (3) Does it introduce framework-wide architectural commitment? (4) Can dependency remain localized to appropriate boundary? (5) Is maintenance/security/licensing acceptable? Do not add packages casually.

engineering/dependencies/domain.md.title: Domain Dependency Discipline
engineering/dependencies/domain.md.first_paragraph: ForgeGate.Domain remains dependency-light. External packages must not leak into Domain without strong architectural reason. Prefer BCL/native value objects and domain logic. Infrastructure/package concerns at natural boundaries.
must_lines: ForgeGate.Domain remains dependency-light. External packages must not leak into Domain without strong architectural reason. Prefer BCL/native value objects and domain logic. Infrastructure/package concerns at natural boundaries.

engineering/dependencies/examples.md.title: Dependency Examples
engineering/dependencies/examples.md.first_paragraph: Reasonable foundational dependencies: EF Core; Npgsql; OpenTelemetry; clearly justified infrastructure libraries. Potential when concrete value demonstrated: FluentValidation; Polly; specialized serializers/helpers. Do NOT introduce by default: AutoMapper; MediatR; generic event-bus frameworks; generic repository frameworks; unnecessary reflection-heavy infrastructure.

engineering/dependencies/management.md.title: Centralized Package Management
engineering/dependencies/management.md.first_paragraph: Manage package versions consistently/centrally to avoid version drift across ForgeGate projects. Use native .NET solution/package-management approach. Do NOT create elaborate dependency tooling solely for this purpose.

engineering/dependencies/policy.md.title: Dependency / Package Policy
engineering/dependencies/policy.md.first_paragraph: Conservative dependency policy. Prefer .NET BCL, ASP.NET Core, first-party/framework capabilities before external package. External dependencies allowed when substantial value and acceptable maintenance/security/licensing. Do NOT introduce package merely to reduce small amount of ordinary code.

engineering/di/di.md.title: Dependency Injection
engineering/di/di.md.first_paragraph: ASP.NET Core DI = application composition mechanism. Constructor-injected dependencies. No service locator, no static mutable services, no manual IServiceProvider resolution from business code, no global singleton accessors. Composition root wires concrete implementations to contracts.

engineering/di/lifetimes.md.title: Service Lifetimes
engineering/di/lifetimes.md.first_paragraph: Not singleton by default. Singleton: process-wide stateless/thread-safe services; intentional process-wide coordinators with protected state; caches. Scoped: request/unit-of-work services; EF Core DbContext; request execution context. Transient: lightweight stateless operations. Every stateful singleton must be thread-safe. Singleton must never depend directly on scoped dependency. Lifetime selected per component during implementation.

engineering/errors/exceptions.md.title: Exceptions
engineering/errors/exceptions.md.first_paragraph: Exceptions for truly unexpected technical failures: programming invariants unexpectedly broken; unexpected serializer/internal failure; infrastructure library failure before normalization. Provider-specific errors normalized at boundary (HttpRequestException → ProviderFailure). Higher-level routing operates on normalized failure concepts.

engineering/errors/handling.md.title: Error Handling
engineering/errors/handling.md.first_paragraph: Exceptions not normal routing/business-control flow. Expected outcomes use explicit result/state models. Exceptions for unexpected exceptional failures. Provider-specific errors normalized at boundary before higher-level routing consumes them. No raw infrastructure exceptions through application logic.

engineering/errors/model.md.title: Application Error / Outcome Model
engineering/errors/model.md.first_paragraph: Hybrid typed-outcome model. Expected business/orchestration conditions use explicit typed results/states. Unexpected technical faults use exceptions. Potential concepts: RouteSelectionResult; CapacityAcquireResult; PolicyEvaluationResult; CompletionAssessment. Not finalized. Expected outcomes (no eligible route; wait required; policy denied; quota exhausted; completion not proven) must not require exception-driven normal control flow.

engineering/errors/result-t.md.title: Do Not Use Result<T> Everywhere
engineering/errors/result-t.md.first_paragraph: Not mechanically wrap every method in Result<T>. Simple deterministic functions/value operations return ordinary values. Explicit outcome types where multiple expected business states meaningful. Avoid both extremes: exceptions for every expected state; Result<T> boilerplate for every trivial method.

engineering/errors/typed-outcomes.md.title: Examples of Expected Typed Outcomes
engineering/errors/typed-outcomes.md.first_paragraph: Conceptual examples (not finalized): RouteSelectionResult; CapacityAcquireResult; PolicyEvaluationResult; CompletionAssessment. Expected states such as no eligible route, wait required, policy denied, quota exhausted, completion not proven should use typed results, not exceptions.

engineering/features/cleanup.md.title: Feature Flag Cleanup
engineering/features/cleanup.md.first_paragraph: Flags are temporary rollout/control mechanisms. When experimental feature stabilizes: make stable behavior default and remove flag; or remove feature. Do NOT accumulate permanent stale flags indefinitely.

engineering/features/flags.md.title: Feature Flag Policy
engineering/features/flags.md.first_paragraph: Feature flags only for risky, experimental or staged runtime capabilities. Examples: semantic policy reasoner; completion verifier; automatic model discovery; experimental provider adapter; advanced supervision; new routing strategy. Not default mechanism for ordinary stable architecture.

engineering/features/not-flagged.md.title: What Should Not Be Feature-Flagged
engineering/features/not-flagged.md.first_paragraph: Not for basic stable concerns: standard validation; canonical request mapping; strongly typed IDs; normal logging; core domain invariants; ordinary mandatory security behavior. Do NOT use flags to compensate for poor modularity.

engineering/features/ownership.md.title: Feature Flag Ownership
engineering/features/ownership.md.first_paragraph: Runtime feature flags belong to operational configuration. Must have: explicit default; clear ownership; observability in Admin where appropriate; audit history for operational changes where appropriate. Avoid flag combinations producing unmanageable state-space complexity.

engineering/health/fail-fast.md.title: Fail-Fast Startup
engineering/health/fail-fast.md.first_paragraph: Mandatory invalid bootstrap configuration must fail startup clearly. Examples: malformed required database config; impossible mandatory internal config; invalid required composition; required schema incompatible with running application where migration policy requires failure. Do NOT silently start partially invalid instance when defect prevents correct operation.

engineering/health/liveness-readiness.md.title: Liveness and Readiness
engineering/health/liveness-readiness.md.first_paragraph: Separate semantics. /liveness → process/application alive. /readiness → ForgeGate initialized sufficiently to service requests as system. Exact endpoint paths follow ASP.NET health-check conventions during implementation, but semantic separation mandatory.

engineering/health/liveness.md.title: Liveness
engineering/health/liveness.md.first_paragraph: Liveness = process/application survival. Must not depend on individual external LLM providers. Example: xKiro unavailable → ForgeGate may still be LIVE. Provider availability belongs to route/provider health.
must_lines: Liveness = process/application survival. Must not depend on individual external LLM providers. Example: xKiro unavailable → ForgeGate may still be LIVE. Provider availability belongs to route/provider health.

engineering/health/provider-failure.md.title: Provider Failure Does Not Automatically Mean Not Ready
engineering/health/provider-failure.md.first_paragraph: Single provider/model route unavailable must not make entire ForgeGate process unready. Example: xKiro unavailable + OpenRouter available → ForgeGate remains ready. Even temporary lack of any currently usable model route is operational routing state, not process/app readiness failure. API/Admin surface may still function correctly and return explicit no-route result.

engineering/health/readiness.md.title: Readiness
engineering/health/readiness.md.first_paragraph: Readiness = whether ForgeGate is operational enough to serve API/control plane according to configured deployment mode. Potential prerequisites: successful application composition/startup; valid mandatory startup config; required persistence availability; required database schema/migrations; required internal invariants initialized. Exact dependency list finalized during implementation.

engineering/health/separate.md.title: Health Semantics Must Remain Separate
engineering/health/separate.md.first_paragraph: Preserve separate concepts: Application liveness; Application readiness; Provider health; ModelRoute health; Capacity/quota state. Do NOT collapse into one universal HealthStatus.
must_lines: # Health Semantics Must Remain Separate

engineering/ids/external.md.title: External Identifiers
engineering/ids/external.md.first_paragraph: Provider-native identifiers may remain provider-native strings when they are external values. Do NOT confuse internal ForgeGate identity with external provider model/resource identifier. Example: ModelRouteId (strongly-typed ForgeGate ID) vs ProviderNativeModelId (provider-owned string/value).

engineering/ids/infrastructure.md.title: Strongly-Typed ID Infrastructure
engineering/ids/infrastructure.md.first_paragraph: Serialization/EF conversion for strongly-typed IDs should be configured centrally/reusably where practical. Do NOT duplicate conversion boilerplate unnecessarily across every entity. Do NOT introduce large reflection/magic framework solely to support ID wrappers.

engineering/ids/strongly-typed.md.title: Strongly-Typed Internal IDs
engineering/ids/strongly-typed.md.first_paragraph: Lightweight strongly-typed IDs for important internal identities. Potential examples: ProviderId; LogicalModelId; ModelRouteId; WorkspaceId; SessionId; RoutingDecisionId; ProviderAttemptId; ActivityEventId. Exact list from implementation. Prefer readonly record struct SessionId(Guid Value) over raw Guid/string everywhere.

engineering/ids/style.md.title: ID Implementation Style
engineering/ids/style.md.first_paragraph: Prefer lightweight value objects (readonly record struct) rather than raw Guid/string everywhere. Goals: compile-time type safety; clearer method signatures; prevention of accidental ID mixing; alignment with thin strict Domain/value-object design. Do NOT build excessive factory/interface/helper infrastructure around IDs.

engineering/immutability/controlled-muta.title: Controlled Mutable Runtime State
engineering/immutability/controlled-muta.first_paragraph: Mutable state allowed where mutation is actual runtime concern. Must expose behavioral APIs rather than public mutable fields/setters. Prefer health.RecordFailure(...); capacity.Acquire(...); capacity.Release(...) rather than health.Failures++; health.State = ...

engineering/immutability/shared-state.md.title: Shared State Ownership
engineering/immutability/shared-state.md.first_paragraph: Every shared mutable runtime concern must have one explicit owner. Conceptual owners: InProcessCapacityCoordinator (capacity/quota/concurrency); ProviderHealthRegistry (provider/model-route health); SessionRuntimeRegistry (active session runtime). Other services must not mutate owner's internal collections directly.

engineering/immutability/strategy.md.title: Immutability Strategy
engineering/immutability/strategy.md.first_paragraph: IMMUTABLE FACTS / VALUE OBJECTS + ENCAPSULATED MUTABLE RUNTIME STATE.

engineering/immutability/thread-safe.md.title: Thread-Safe State Owners
engineering/immutability/thread-safe.md.first_paragraph: Shared-state owners responsible for their own concurrency safety. Implementation details: lock; SemaphoreSlim; ConcurrentDictionary; Channel; Interlocked; other .NET primitives. Primitive is implementation detail. Do NOT expose mutable dictionaries/collections for external mutation. No actor framework in MVP solely for concurrency control.

engineering/implementation-phase.md.title: Implementation Phase Rule
engineering/implementation-phase.md.first_paragraph: High-level product architecture and core code-architecture baseline now sufficiently defined. From this point: do not expand architecture speculatively; resolve detailed design questions just-in-time per implementation slice; prefer runtime proof over further abstract planning; keep each slice narrow; preserve all documented architecture rules; if slice exposes missing architectural decision, stop only for that specific decision, document it, then continue.

engineering/mapping/no-automapper.md.title: No AutoMapper by Default
engineering/mapping/no-automapper.md.first_paragraph: No AutoMapper/reflection-based mapping as default architecture. Important semantic transformations must remain visible and debuggable. For tiny pure value conversions, small pure/static mapper acceptable. Do NOT create one class merely because every mapping must have a class.

engineering/mapping/translation.md.title: Mapping / Translation
engineering/mapping/translation.md.first_paragraph: Explicit mapping/translation at architectural boundaries. Conceptual pipeline: OpenAI DTO → explicit protocol mapper → canonical ForgeGate model → provider request normalizer → provider transport → provider response normalizer → canonical ForgeGate response → explicit OpenAI response mapper.

engineering/notifications/control-flow.m.title: Control Flow Must Remain Explicit
engineering/notifications/control-flow.m.first_paragraph: If correctness requires an operation, invoke explicitly. Route selection, capacity acquisition, provider execution, required policy enforcement must remain visible in main orchestration path. Do NOT hide mandatory steps behind event handlers.

engineering/notifications/no-event-bus.m.title: No Enterprise Event Bus in MVP
engineering/notifications/no-event-bus.m.first_paragraph: No RabbitMQ, Kafka, distributed message bus, complex delivery semantics, generic enterprise event framework, MediatR solely for notifications. If small in-process publisher/dispatcher abstraction useful, keep it minimal.

engineering/notifications/notifications..title: Internal Notifications
engineering/notifications/notifications..first_paragraph: Explicit direct calls for critical control flow. Lightweight typed in-process notifications for secondary reactions. Potential notification concepts: ProviderAttemptCompleted; RoutingDecisionMade; PolicyDecisionMade; CompletionAssessmentCreated. Exact types NOT finalized. Notifications for independent secondary effects (audit/activity, projection updates, health state, metrics). Not for hiding mandatory execution steps.

engineering/nullability/explicit.md.title: Explicit Optionality
engineering/nullability/explicit.md.first_paragraph: If absence has meaningful domain/application semantics, model that semantic state explicitly where appropriate. Examples: Unknown; NotObserved; Unavailable; NotApplicable — should not automatically be encoded as null when distinction matters.

engineering/nullability/normalization.md.title: External Nullability Normalization
engineering/nullability/normalization.md.first_paragraph: External/provider DTOs may naturally contain many nullable/optional fields. Normalize them early at their boundary. Canonical/application models should generally be stricter than raw external DTOs. Example: provider raw response (nullable/loose) → ProviderResponseNormalizer → canonical response (validated/normalized/stronger invariants).

engineering/nullability/strict.md.title: Nullability
engineering/nullability/strict.md.first_paragraph: Strict nullable-reference-type semantics enabled. null represents actual contract-level absence, not undocumented generic "unknown state".

engineering/observability/channels.md.title: Observability Channels
engineering/observability/channels.md.first_paragraph: Separate concerns: Technical diagnostics → ILogger / structured logs. Durable business/audit facts → ActivityEvent / persistence. Metrics → counters / histograms / gauges. Distributed/request tracing → OpenTelemetry spans. Do NOT use one channel for all purposes.

engineering/observability/correlation.md.title: Correlation Context
engineering/observability/correlation.md.first_paragraph: Observability channels share correlation identifiers where available. Potential examples: RequestId; SessionId; WorkspaceId; ProviderAttemptId; RoutingDecisionId. Allows logs, traces, activity facts, metrics to be correlated. Secrets/sensitive payloads must not leak through correlation/observability.

engineering/observability/logs-vs-audit..title: Logs Are Not Audit
engineering/observability/logs-vs-audit..first_paragraph: ILogger output = technical diagnostic information, not authoritative audit history. ActivityEvent must not become dumping ground for stack traces and low-level debug noise.
must_lines: ILogger output = technical diagnostic information, not authoritative audit history. ActivityEvent must not become dumping ground for stack traces and low-level debug noise.

engineering/observability/open-telemetry.title: Open Telemetry
engineering/observability/open-telemetry.first_paragraph: Preferred future tracing/metrics interoperability approach. Do not over-instrument every method. Trace meaningful operation boundaries: inbound gateway request; route selection; capacity wait/acquire; provider attempt; policy evaluation; completion verification. Exact instrumentation = implementation work.

engineering/persistence/boundary.md.title: Persistence Boundary
engineering/persistence/boundary.md.first_paragraph: Application must not depend directly on EF Core DbContext. No generic Repository<T>. No UnitOfWork wrapper solely for pattern compliance. Focused persistence ports per feature/use case. Examples: IActivityStore.AppendAsync(...), IActivityStore.QueryRecentAsync(...); ISessionStore.GetAsync(...), ISessionStore.SaveAsync(...). Not IRepository<T>.GetAll/Insert/Update/Delete. No IQueryable or EF-specific concepts in Application contracts.

engineering/persistence/ports.md.title: Persistence Ports Are Intent-Oriented
engineering/persistence/ports.md.first_paragraph: Contracts expose operations meaningful to consumer. Prefer feature-oriented ports (IActivityStore, ISessionStore, IRoutingConfigStore, IProviderConfigStore) with semantic methods. Avoid generic repository abstraction. Implementation details (EF, PostgreSQL) stay in Infrastructure.

engineering/providers/extensibility.md.title: Provider Extensibility
engineering/providers/extensibility.md.first_paragraph: New provider requires: provider-specific adapter/transport; provider-specific normalization; capability/config registration; error mapping. Must NOT require editing routing core with provider-name conditionals. Provider quirks remain local to provider infrastructure boundaries.

engineering/providers/implementation.md.title: Provider Implementation Structure
engineering/providers/implementation.md.first_paragraph: Each provider has local provider-specific infrastructure module/folder (Infrastructure/Providers/OpenRouter/, XKiro/, Vireonix/). Includes transport/config; request normalization; response normalization; failure mapping; quirks. Shared OpenAI-compatible plumbing under Infrastructure/Providers/Common/ (HTTP plumbing, serialization, SSE parsing, reusable transport). Provider quirks remain local. No provider-name conditionals in routing/application.

engineering/serialization/contracts.md.title: Serialization Contract Ownership
engineering/serialization/contracts.md.first_paragraph: Serialized contracts belong to their boundary. OpenAI transport DTOs → Api/Protocol boundary. Provider payloads → Infrastructure/Providers/<Provider>. Admin HTTP DTOs → Admin/API boundary. Internal application/domain models → not automatically persistence DTOs. Do NOT reuse one DTO everywhere merely to reduce mapping code.

engineering/serialization/version-only.m.title: Version Only Stable Boundaries
engineering/serialization/version-only.m.first_paragraph: Do NOT version every internal record/class. Versioning required where compatibility matters across time/system boundaries: durable polymorphic activity payloads; external/admin contracts where backward compatibility promised. Internal temporary implementation models may evolve normally.

engineering/serialization/versioning.md.title: Durable Payload Versioning
engineering/serialization/versioning.md.first_paragraph: Serialized payloads stored durably and expected to survive application versions should support explicit type/schema versioning where needed. Conceptual: ActivityEvent Type = "routing.decision" Version = 1 Payload = ... Exact representation not finalized.

engineering/solid/alignment.md.title: OOP / SOLID Alignment
engineering/solid/alignment.md.first_paragraph: Newer decisions reinforce previously documented mandatory engineering principles: OOP; SOLID; Dependency Injection; Replaceable Components; Explicit Contracts; Focused Responsibilities; Thread Safety for Shared State; Testability. Replaceability does NOT mean maximum abstraction count.

engineering/solid/solid.md.title: SOLID
engineering/solid/solid.md.first_paragraph: SRP: one coherent reason to change (routing, failure normalization, provider transport, capability evaluation, capacity, policy, completion verification separate). OCP: extensible through composition/implementations, not central switch edits. LSP: implementations preserve contracts. ISP: small focused contracts, not giant ILLMProvider with Chat/Stream/ListModels/GetQuota/Health/Vision/Tools. DIP: higher-level logic depends on abstractions, not concrete provider/DB/secret implementations.

engineering/style/architecture.md.title: Architectural Style
engineering/style/architecture.md.first_paragraph: MODULAR MONOLITH + CLEAN / HEXAGONAL DEPENDENCY BOUNDARIES + FEATURE-ORIENTED INTERNAL STRUCTURE. MVP remains one deployable application. Strong module boundaries for future evolution/replacement. No microservices.

engineering/style/code-quality.md.title: Code Quality Rule
engineering/style/code-quality.md.first_paragraph: When changing an area: (1) identify responsibility boundary; (2) preserve/improve OOP/SOLID separation; (3) if mixed responsibilities or poor replaceability, perform smallest safe structural refactor required; (4) do not refactor unrelated modules; (5) verify behavior after change. Architectural quality improves incrementally without broad speculative rewrites.

engineering/style/concurrency.md.title: Concurrency
engineering/style/concurrency.md.first_paragraph: Multi-session and concurrent by design. Any process-wide mutable service must be explicitly thread-safe. No accidental mutable global collections. Concurrency semantics required for CapacityCoordinator, health state, active sessions, provider runtime state, workspace coordination. Thread safety is part of contract, not afterthought.

engineering/style/domain-thin.md.title: Domain Layer: Thin and Strict
engineering/style/domain-thin.md.first_paragraph: Only concepts with genuine independent domain meaning/invariants belong in Domain. Potential examples: LogicalModel; ModelRoute identity/value concepts; Capability requirements; routing profile rules/value concepts; PolicyDecision value concepts; CompletionStatus; WorkspaceId; SessionId. Exact classes during implementation. Do NOT move something to Domain merely because it sounds business-related.

engineering/style/feature-oriented.md.title: Feature-Oriented Internal Structure
engineering/style/feature-oriented.md.first_paragraph: Inside Application/Domain/Infrastructure, prefer grouping by capability/feature rather than generic technical buckets. Conceptual structure: Application/Routing/, Providers/, Capacity/, Sessions/, Policy/, Completion/; Infrastructure/Providers/Common/, OpenRouter/, XKiro/, Vireonix/, Persistence/, Secrets/. Not Services/Managers/Helpers/Utils.

engineering/style/no-god-service.md.title: No God Gateway Service

Coordinator may have several collaborators when real use case requires, but responsibilities remain separated.

engineering/style/no-mediatr.md.title: No Mandatory MediatR / CQRS
engineering/style/no-mediatr.md.first_paragraph: No MediatR or CQRS framework merely to organize use cases. Command/handler patterns only if concrete complexity justifies. MVP uses direct explicit application services/coordinators.

engineering/style/no-premature.md.title: No Premature Enterprise Abstractions
engineering/style/no-premature.md.first_paragraph: Strong OOP/SOLID does not mean unnecessary frameworks. Do NOT add by default: MediatR; CQRS framework; generic Repository<T>; UnitOfWork wrapper over EF Core solely for pattern compliance; event bus with no real need; microservices; Redis; distributed messaging; reflection-heavy plugin system; generic policy/routing DSL. Introduce patterns only when actual ForgeGate requirement justifies them.

engineering/style/not-domain.md.title: What Does Not Belong in Domain
engineering/style/not-domain.md.first_paragraph: Application orchestration; ChatExecutionService; provider execution; SessionResolver workflow; HTTP/OpenAI DTOs; EF Core entities/config; provider transports; persistence queries; external integration details. If a type exists mainly because a use case must be executed, it is usually Application rather than Domain.

engineering/style/project-structure-top..title: Top-Level Project Structure

engineering/style/project-structure.md.title: Domain / Application / Infrastructure / API / Admin
engineering/style/project-structure.md.first_paragraph: Domain: core business concepts/invariants without infrastructure. Application: use cases; orchestration of domain capabilities; ports/contracts; application-level decisions. Infrastructure: provider HTTP integrations; EF Core/PostgreSQL; secret-store implementations; external adapters. Api: HTTP/OpenAI-compatible protocol layer; transport validation; DI composition/startup; OpenAPI. Admin: React/TypeScript operational control-plane UI.

engineering/style/replaceability-expecta.title: Replaceability Expectation
engineering/style/replaceability-expecta.first_paragraph: Important subsystem implementations replaceable primarily through composition/config change + new implementation, not unrelated module edits. Examples: EnvironmentSecretStore → KeychainSecretStore; InProcessCapacityCoordinator → distributed coordinator; provider adapter implementation; EF persistence adapter → alternate persistence where required.

engineering/style/replaceability-test.md.title: Architectural Replaceability Test
engineering/style/replaceability-test.md.first_paragraph: Mental test: "If this implementation replaced tomorrow, how much unrelated code changes?" Desired: composition/config changes + new implementation, not edits throughout unrelated code. Design heuristic, not mandate to abstract every class.

engineering/style/replaceability.md.title: Replaceability
engineering/style/replaceability.md.first_paragraph: Important subsystems must be replaceable without rewriting unrelated code. Examples: provider adapter; SecretStore; CapacityCoordinator; persistence; Semantic Policy Reasoner.
must_lines: Important subsystems must be replaceable without rewriting unrelated code. Examples: provider adapter; SecretStore; CapacityCoordinator; persistence; Semantic Policy Reasoner.

engineering/style/style.md.title: Core Engineering Style
engineering/style/style.md.first_paragraph: Strong OOP + SOLID. Encapsulation, explicit responsibilities, dependency inversion, interface segregation, composition over hidden coupling, replaceable components, testable boundaries, cohesive classes/modules, explicit contracts.

engineering/testing/architecture.md.title: Test Architecture
engineering/testing/architecture.md.first_paragraph: Test pyramid: Domain/value objects → unit tests. Application logic → focused unit/contract tests through fake/test implementations of ports. Infrastructure adapters → integration/fixture-based tests. OpenAI gateway vertical paths → small number of end-to-end tests. Not almost exclusively mocks; not almost exclusively expensive E2E.

engineering/testing/provider-fixtures.md.title: Provider Test Fixtures
engineering/testing/provider-fixtures.md.first_paragraph: Provider integration testing should support deterministic fixtures/synthetic payloads. Examples: provider success response fixtures; normalized failure fixtures; malformed response fixtures; tool-call fixtures; streaming/SSE fixtures; quota/rate-limit fixtures. Provider adapters should not require real external API call for every ordinary CI test.

engineering/testing/real-provider.md.title: Real Provider Tests
engineering/testing/real-provider.md.first_paragraph: Tests calling real external providers must be: explicitly opt-in; separated from normal deterministic CI; clearly identified as integration/live tests; safe regarding credentials/rate limits. Standard test suite must not depend on free provider availability.

engineering/testing/regression.md.title: Focused Regression Tests
engineering/testing/regression.md.first_paragraph: Bug fixes and contract corrections should include focused regression test when practical. Broad passing suite does not replace missing focused evidence. Each focused test should make contract clear: Given / When / Then. Aligns with agent execution evidence rules.

engineering/tests/testability.md.title: Testability
engineering/tests/testability.md.first_paragraph: Important behavior testable without real external providers. Important components support deterministic tests with substitute implementations at architectural boundaries. Router with fake route state; CapacityCoordinator without real provider; Policy without real VS Code client; failure normalization with fixtures; provider adapters separately from routing. Design around meaningful contracts; testability follows from boundaries. Not design around mocks.

engineering/transactions/external-io.md.title: External I/O and Database Transactions
engineering/transactions/external-io.md.first_paragraph: Do NOT hold long-running DB transactions around LLM provider calls, external HTTP calls, user interaction, long waits, capacity waiting. Do NOT attempt distributed ACID between PostgreSQL and external providers. Use appropriate explicit consistency/eventual patterns where needed.

engineering/transactions/narrow.md.title: Narrow Explicit Transaction Boundaries
engineering/transactions/narrow.md.first_paragraph: Where several persistence operations must be atomic, use explicit narrow transaction/consistency boundary appropriate to that use case. No generic UnitOfWork solely for pattern compliance. Exact transaction contract created only when real atomic multi-store use case requires it.

engineering/transactions/ownership.md.title: Database Transaction Ownership
engineering/transactions/ownership.md.first_paragraph: Transaction boundaries determined by use-case consistency requirement. Not automatically: each repository call = own transaction; each HTTP request = one giant DB transaction; every use case = generic UnitOfWork.

engineering/validation/domain-invariants.title: Domain Invariants
engineering/validation/domain-invariants.first_paragraph: Important value/domain invariants must remain inside value/domain concept. Example: invalid SessionId or invalid domain value should not require every caller to remember external validation service. Factories/constructors may enforce invariants. Do NOT force transport/provider validation into Domain.

engineering/validation/libraries.md.title: Validation Libraries
engineering/validation/libraries.md.first_paragraph: FluentValidation or similar may be used where they provide real value. Not mandatory architectural dependency. Do not force all validation through one framework.

engineering/validation/ownership.md.title: Validation Ownership
engineering/validation/ownership.md.first_paragraph: Validation belongs to architectural boundary that owns the rule. Conceptual ownership: API boundary → transport/schema/request validation; Protocol Adapter → protocol semantic/normalization validation; Domain/value objects → domain invariants; Application/use case → use-case preconditions; Provider/route boundary → capability/compatibility validation; Startup/config → configuration validation. No universal validation layer.

frontend-code-style.md.title: Frontend code style
frontend-code-style.md.first_paragraph: Канон фронтенд-стилю для **dochub-site** (Cloudflare Pages + React + TypeScript).

health/composite.md.title: Composite Route Health
health/composite.md.first_paragraph: Not boolean. Composite dimensions conceptually: AvailabilityState; CredentialState; CapacityState; QuotaState; RecentFailureState; cooldown info; last observation timestamp. Example: Availability=Reachable, Credential=Valid, Capacity=TemporarilyLimited, Quota=Available, RecentFailure=RateLimited → route not globally dead. Exact enums NOT frozen.

health/passive-first.md.title: Passive-First Health Observation
health/passive-first.md.first_paragraph: Production traffic is primary health evidence. Active probes selective: route unused long period; cooldown expired and recovery needs verification; provider exposes useful explicit health endpoint; discovery/admin validation requires it. Avoid probe spam, especially against free providers.

models/route-responsibilities.md.title: Model Route Responsibilities
models/route-responsibilities.md.first_paragraph: ModelRoute may carry: provider-native model identifier; declared capabilities; observed capabilities; context limit; provider-specific constraints; health; capacity/quota scope; enabled state; priority/quality override; observed reliability; provider quirks. Do NOT duplicate provider-global facts unnecessarily. Exact ownership finalized during implementation.

persistence/boundary.md.title: PostgreSQL Persistence Boundary
persistence/boundary.md.first_paragraph: Durable structured facts + configurable/selective raw payload retention. Not almost nothing; not everything forever.

persistence/facts-vs-projections.md.title: Durable Facts vs Derived Projections
persistence/facts-vs-projections.md.first_paragraph: Durable structured facts → derived projections/session views/policy context.

persistence/retention.md.title: Raw Payload Retention
persistence/retention.md.first_paragraph: Configurable retention modes (names/config not finalized): Off; MetadataOnly; Redacted; Full.
must_lines: Default: bounded/minimal retention. Full/debug enabled deliberately. Security/privacy implications must be considered.

policy/correction-loop.md.title: Integration with Internal Correction Loop
policy/correction-loop.md.first_paragraph: Denied/rejected candidate action fed back internally to same model with bounded corrective context so model can replan. Conceptual flow: model → candidate → policy denial → ForgeGate corrective feedback → same model replans → policy evaluates again. Retry/replan loops bounded. Internal correction turns not exposed to client as ordinary assistant output unless protocol/failure handling requires.

policy/deterministic-first.md.title: Deterministic-First Policy
policy/deterministic-first.md.first_paragraph: Obvious violations handled without semantic LLM reasoning. Initial high-value examples: unsafe git recovery operations; destructive broad filesystem operations; obvious certification manipulation patterns; explicit policy-prohibited commands. Aligns with real-world agent failure-pattern requirements.

policy/mvp-scope.md.title: MVP Tool Supervision Scope
policy/mvp-scope.md.first_paragraph: Not all future agent-supervision rules immediately. MVP prioritizes: structural validation; high-value deterministic safety/workspace rules; basic cross-session protection; bounded semantic escalation for suspicious actions; clear policy decision logging. Full Investigation Supervisor / complete behavioral rule library deferred.

policy/outcomes.md.title: Policy Decision Outcomes
policy/outcomes.md.first_paragraph: Conceptual outcomes: ALLOW; DENY; REPLAN; ASK_USER. DENY (action must not execute) and REPLAN (model should choose another compliant path) are different concepts. Exact enum/internal protocol NOT finalized.

policy/pre-execution.md.title: Pre-Execution Enforcement
policy/pre-execution.md.first_paragraph: Policy evaluates candidate tool action BEFORE committed to client for execution whenever protocol/tool flow permits.

policy/semantic-escalation.md.title: Semantic Escalation
policy/semantic-escalation.md.first_paragraph: Semantic reasoner used only when deterministic rules cannot safely resolve intent/proportionality. Examples: Python script rewriting one line instead of native edit; bulk script over many files where automation appropriate; indirect mutation mechanisms; likely circumvention of previously rejected action; ambiguous cross-session mutation. Contextual and bounded. Not required for routine safe actions (ordinary reads/status checks).

policy/structural-validation.md.title: Structural Tool Validation
policy/structural-validation.md.first_paragraph: Before policy reasoning: tool exists in exposed tool set; arguments valid enough for declared schema; tool-call structure complete; malformed partial streaming fragments not released as executable calls. Exact validation library/schema mechanics = implementation decision.

policy/tool-enforcement.md.title: Tool-Call Validation and Policy Enforcement
policy/tool-enforcement.md.first_paragraph: Layered enforcement: structural validation → deterministic policy → suspicion/risk signal → semantic reasoner only when needed → ALLOW / DENY / REPLAN / ASK_USER. Not deterministic-only long-term; not LLM reasoner for every call.

protocol/canonical-model.md.title: Internal Canonical Request/Response Model
protocol/canonical-model.md.first_paragraph: Application/core logic operates on protocol-neutral canonical request/response concepts, not directly on OpenAI transport DTOs. Exact DTO/schema NOT finalized. Must eventually support routing, capability validation, policy, tool calls, usage, streaming, provider normalization. Do NOT overgeneralize for every future protocol yet.

protocol/openai-compat.md.first_paragraph: MVP external contract: GET /v1/models, POST /v1/chat/completions (Chat Completions family only). Supports non-streaming, streaming, system/user/assistant/tool messages, tool calls/tool_choice, model selection, common generation parameters, OpenAI-like error behavior.

providers/capability-based.md.title: Capability-Based Provider Abstraction
providers/capability-based.md.first_paragraph: Avoid giant universal provider interface with optional/null methods. Avoid provider-specific HTTP/error/model quirks leaking into routing core.

providers/failure-taxonomy.md.title: Normalized Provider Failure Taxonomy
providers/failure-taxonomy.md.first_paragraph: Normalized categories (conceptual, may evolve): AuthenticationFailed; AuthorizationFailed; RateLimited; QuotaExhausted; ConcurrencyLimited; ProviderUnavailable; Timeout; NetworkFailure; ModelUnavailable; InvalidModel; CapabilityUnsupported; ContextExceeded; InvalidRequest; MalformedResponse; StreamInterrupted; UnknownProviderFailure.

providers/quirk-profiles.md.title: Quirk Profiles / Normalization Hooks
providers/quirk-profiles.md.first_paragraph: Potential quirks: custom headers; unusual model IDs; missing usage; non-standard finish reasons; slightly non-standard SSE; tool-call shape variations; request parameter differences. Architecture provides explicit local extension points. No generic provider-quirk DSL in MVP. Simple provider-local code/config sufficient.

providers/quirks.md.title: Provider-Specific Quirks
providers/quirks.md.first_paragraph: Provider-specific compatibility behavior localized at provider adapter/normalization boundary. No `if provider == xKiro` through routing/core/application logic.

providers/retryability.md.title: Retryability and Failure Scope
providers/retryability.md.first_paragraph: Category alone insufficient. Must understand: immediately retryable; retryable after delay; retryable through another provider; not retryable without config/user intervention.
must_lines: Category alone insufficient. Must understand: immediately retryable; retryable after delay; retryable through another provider; not retryable without config/user intervention.

quality/future.md.title: Future Adaptive Quality
quality/future.md.first_paragraph: Defer: automatic quality benchmarking; automatic model tier reassignment; coding/reasoning benchmark suite; learned adaptive model scoring; auto-tuning from historical outcomes. Observed signals should make these possible later.

quality/model.md.title: Model Quality Model
quality/model.md.first_paragraph: MVP: manual declared quality baseline + observed runtime performance signals. Not full automatic benchmarking/reclassification.
must_lines: DeclaredQualityTier (manual/admin). ObservedPerformance: latency, failure rate, tool-call validity, policy violation frequency, completion-success signals, other operational observations. Observed performance may affect operational ranking.

routing/decision.md.title: Routing Decision as First-Class Fact
routing/decision.md.first_paragraph: Every route selection produces compact RoutingDecision. Do NOT persist full verbose candidate graph for every normal request by default.

routing/profiles.md.title: Routing Profiles
routing/profiles.md.first_paragraph: Existing profiles: forgegate/fast, balanced, smart, coding. Control wait tolerance, degradation tolerance, minimum quality floor, routing behavior. Numeric values remain configuration, not architectural constants.

routing/strategy.md.title: Routing Strategy
routing/strategy.md.first_paragraph: Hard eligibility filters → quality tier → simple operational ranking. Not one opaque universal numeric score.

routing/substitution.md.title: Explainable Substitution
routing/substitution.md.first_paragraph: When preferred route skipped, retain reason. Conceptual: preferred skipped: CAPABILITY_MISMATCH(tools). Substitution policy: same logical model, different provider → normally automatic; different model, same quality tier → generally automatic per profile; lower quality tier → DEGRADE / ASK_USER per policy; no eligible route → explicit capability/routing failure. Observable in audit/admin.

routing/user-interaction.md.title: User Interaction on Significant Degradation
routing/user-interaction.md.first_paragraph: ASK_USER appropriate when downgrade significant for current task and client supports ask-user capability. Minor route changes (same logical model through another provider) may be automatic. Do NOT assume all OpenAI-compatible clients expose native ask-user tool.

routing/verbose-trace.md.title: Optional Verbose Routing Trace
routing/verbose-trace.md.first_paragraph: Detailed candidate analysis retained when useful: debug mode; routing failure; degradation; ASK_USER; unexpected route choice; admin drill-down. Verbose trace = secondary/debug evidence. Compact RoutingDecision = canonical normal routing fact.

routing/wait-switch-degrade.md.title: Wait / Switch / Degrade Policy
routing/wait-switch-degrade.md.first_paragraph: Profile-driven wait budget + degradation budget + task-aware quality floor. Not always fail over immediately; not always wait indefinitely.

secrets/references.md.title: Database Stores Credential References
secrets/references.md.first_paragraph: ProviderConfig references credentials indirectly (e.g., CredentialRef = "xkiro-main"). Actual secret resolved through secret-store abstraction. Raw provider API keys must not be embedded in normal persisted provider configuration.

secrets/safety.md.title: Secret Safety Requirements
secrets/safety.md.first_paragraph: Secrets must never appear in: activity logs; audit events; raw provider error storage; telemetry; config exports; admin API responses. Raw upstream errors require redaction before durable logging. Admin UI displays secrets masked/opaque. Public repo contains only safe examples (`.env.example`), never real credentials. supervision/completion-verification.md.title: Completion Verification
supervision/completion-verification.md.first_paragraph: Separate concern from Action Policy.
